newsitem.title: USA: Republicans push bill to limit volunteer suits.
newsitem.headline: Republicans push bill to limit volunteer suits.

text.p: Saying Girl Scout and Little League groups were at risk across the nation, Speaker Newt Gingrich Wednesday vowed the House would quickly pass a bill to protect volunteers from nuisance lawsuits.
Gingrich made his comments as House and Senate Republicans opened their drive for a bill shielding community volunteers from lawsuits, except for cases of willful or wanton misconduct.

"You shouldn't have to go to somebody and have their first question be in a free society, 'What is my liability risk?'" Gingrich told a news conference. "Our job in the Congress is to make volunteerism easier and more desirable."
The Georgia Republican took a swipe at U.S. trial lawyers, who have given millions of dollars to Democrats, accusing them of creating a culture of litigation.

"The simple fact is that there has emerged a predatory culture of trial lawyers that has fought for and maintained a system of blackmail and a system of negotiated settlements that is simply wrong," Gingrich said.
Supporters cited anecdotal evidence and limited studies to support their case. For instance, they said Little League liability costs rose more than 1,000 percent in the mid to late 1980s.
They also claimed local Girl Scouts had to sell tens of thousands of boxes of cookies to cover their liability costs.

The legislation has been endorsed by a host of community groups. But in testimony prepared for a hearing, Andrew Popper, professor of law at American University in Washington questioned whether it was necessary.

He said one version of the volunteer legislation, which would pre-empt state laws, was troubling in the absence of any studies showing there was a national crisis. He also said the exemptions appeared to be broad.
